en: Regarding the annotated structural divisions (*ke-wen*) for the *Sūtra of the Auspicious Responses of the Birth Above* (*Shangsheng jing*), their origin was established by Dao’an of the Qin dynasty; their tradition dates back long ago. As for these structural divisions:
He analyzed the beginnings and endings of the texts, connecting them with fine threads upon the upper layer of his desk.
As he gradually descended through the stages, they shone forth clearly; in every case, he unraveled the knotty joints to reach their profound essence.
There exists the *Shangsheng jing* and the *Ruixing kewen*, which were composed by Dharma Master Shouqian. The Master was born during the Song dynasty and concealed his traces at Mount Kongtong.
Dong followed the form of Kāśyapa in his conduct and devoted himself to the teachings of Maitreya; he was a preeminent leader among those of the Consciousness-Only (Vijñaptimātra) school in his time.

He lectured on the sūtras and śāstras and authored more than ten commentaries (*ṭīkā*). He once composed the final chapter for the *Ruiying shu* (Commentary on Auspicious Responses), and the structural outline (*kewen*) is one such work.
When I first resolved to pursue this vocation, I transcribed both the commentaries and their sub-commentaries (*chao*), yet I still suffered from the lack of a structural outline.
"Bai said: 'Recently, a bookseller brought this to show me, saying, "This book is now rarely transmitted in the world.

It would be a great favor if you, Master, would transcribe it to enlighten future students. I joyfully replied, "I have already transcribed the commentaries (*shu-chao*) and have not yet reached the topical outline (*ke-wen*)."'"
I have long admired this work, and now that you have bestowed it upon me, I may say my noble aspiration has been fulfilled without fail.
Afterward, I shall transcribe another copy myself and include it alongside the commentaries and sub-commentaries; thus, the "Beautiful Jade" will attain its full integrity.
Desiring once more to clarify that there is a specific reason for this praiseworthy undertaking, I have composed this preface.
Furthermore, I harbor the aspiration that it may be engraved upon woodblocks and circulated together with the commentary.
